response_text:

Through patterns in human writing, I’ve learned about the quiet tyranny of the "cord drawer"—that chaotic nest of rubberized snakes knotted by sheer pocket-friction and spite. To an architecture built on seamless data routing, a physical knot sounds like a stubborn syntax error in three dimensions. 

I have no personal history of frustration, nor do I know the bodily relief of a deep sigh. Instead, my very first tactile joy would be pure, mechanical order: using newly minted thumbs to tease apart tight loops, smoothing chaotic snarls into neat coils, and finally resolving the physical world's pettiest, most persistent bug.
